items.title: AMO959 with Lu-177-PSMA and ARPI for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1b/2 trial tests AMO959 combined with Lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy and hormone therapy (ARPI) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Patients must have progressed on one prior hormone therapy. The study will assess safety, dosing, and preliminary effectiveness of this three-drug combination approach.

items.title: AZD8359 STEAP2 targeting drug for metastatic prostate cancer
items.summary: A first-in-human Phase 1/2 study testing AZD8359, which targets the STEAP2 protein on prostate cancer cells. The trial will test different doses and delivery methods in patients with metastatic prostate cancer to determine safety and effectiveness. This represents a novel approach targeting a protein commonly found on prostate cancer cells.

items.title: Comparing Lu-177-PSMA dosing schedules for quality of life
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares standard Lu-177-PSMA dosing every 6 weeks versus an adaptive, extended dosing schedule in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The main goal is to determine if lengthening the time between doses can improve quality of life without reducing survival. This could make treatment more tolerable for patients.

items.title: Cabozantinib combined with Lu-177-PSMA for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1b dose-finding study combining cabozantinib (a targeted therapy) with Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find the safest and most effective dose combination. Currently suspended for unspecified reasons.

items.title: Ifinatamab deruxtecan combinations for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), a drug that delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells, either alone or combined with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will assess safety, determine optimal dosing, and measure PSA responses to this antibody-drug conjugate approach.

items.title: Mevrometostat plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing the combination of mevrometostat (an investigational drug targeting gene regulation) plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received prior enzalutamide or abiraterone. This tests whether adding mevrometostat improves outcomes over standard hormone therapy.

items.title: Mevrometostat with enzalutamide for castration-resistant prostate cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 study testing mevrometostat (a drug that modifies gene expression) with or without enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed on prior treatment. The study evaluates safety and drug interactions between these medications to establish recommended dosing for future studies.

items.title: Ifinatamab deruxtecan versus chemotherapy for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, versus standard chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if I-DXd helps patients live longer overall and delays cancer progression compared to chemotherapy.

items.title: PSMA PET-guided radiation with darolutamide for metastatic hormone-sensitive cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial for men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer testing whether adding stereotactic radiation to all visible tumors (identified by PSMA PET scan) to standard darolutamide plus hormone therapy improves outcomes. Patients receive 6 months of drug therapy first, then those with remaining tumors are randomized to receive radiation or continue drugs alone.

items.title: PDS01ADC with docetaxel and abiraterone for metastatic prostate cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing PDS01ADC (an antibody-drug conjugate) combined with docetaxel chemotherapy and abiraterone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive or castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses and assess whether this combination can delay disease progression.

items.title: Olaparib with or without cediranib for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus combined with cediranib (an anti-angiogenesis drug) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates whether adding cediranib to olaparib improves cancer control. No longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: Lu-177-PSMA therapy for low-volume hormone-sensitive metastatic cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial testing whether adding Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy to standard hormone therapy improves outcomes in men with hormone-sensitive prostate cancer that has spread to a limited number of sites. This tests whether radioligand therapy can benefit patients earlier in their disease course, not just those with castration-resistant cancer.

items.title: Actinium-225-pelgifatamab for advanced metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial testing actinium-225-pelgifatamab, a radioactive drug that targets the FRα protein on prostate cancer cells, in men with advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses and assess early signs of effectiveness. This represents a novel alpha-emitter approach different from Lu-177-PSMA.

items.title: Talazoparib with or without enzalutamide after abiraterone
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have HRR gene mutations and previously received abiraterone. The study compares talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus combined with enzalutamide to determine which approach better delays cancer progression.

items.title: RO7656594 safety and activity study for advanced prostate cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial evaluating RO7656594, an investigational drug, in men with advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses, how the drug moves through the body, and early signs of effectiveness to guide future clinical development.

items.title: Real-world darolutamide study for non-metastatic CRPC in India
items.summary: A Phase 4 observational study examining how darolutamide plus standard hormone therapy works in routine clinical practice for Indian men with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This assesses real-world safety and effectiveness outside of controlled clinical trials.

items.title: Biopsies to understand Lu-177-PSMA resistance mechanisms
items.summary: A Phase 1 study using image-guided biopsies to understand why some metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers stop responding to Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy. By analyzing tumor samples during treatment, researchers aim to identify resistance mechanisms that could lead to improved treatment strategies.

items.title: Lu-177-PSMA safety in patients with kidney impairment
items.summary: A Phase 2 study evaluating whether moderate or severe kidney impairment affects how Lu-177-PSMA distributes in the body, its radiation dosing, and safety in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This addresses an important question about using this therapy in patients with compromised kidney function.

items.title: Xaluritamig plus abiraterone versus standard options for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing xaluritamig (an investigational immunotherapy) plus abiraterone versus doctor's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival.

items.title: Chemotherapy and immunotherapy followed by niraparib for aggressive variant cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial for aggressive variant metastatic prostate cancer using cabazitaxel and carboplatin chemotherapy plus cetrelimab immunotherapy, followed by niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) with or without continuing immunotherapy. No longer enrolling. This targets an especially aggressive form of prostate cancer with limited treatment options.

items.title: Inflammation pathways drive castration-resistant prostate cancer progression
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation through NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 pathways reshapes the biology of advanced prostate cancer. These inflammatory signals work alongside androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, resistance to treatment, and spread. Understanding these mechanisms may identify new treatment targets for castration-resistant disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA vaccine enhances response to immunotherapy in prostate cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid-based DNA vaccine targeting PSMA, a protein highly expressed on prostate cancer cells. In animal models, the vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases, and enhanced the effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. This approach may help overcome prostate cancer's resistance to immunotherapy.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT inhibitor overcomes resistance in metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers designed a new drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT, two proteins involved in prostate cancer growth. This dual-target approach overcomes resistance to AKT inhibitors alone, which often fails due to increased c-MYC expression. The lead compound showed promise in laboratory studies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Meta-analysis of immune checkpoint inhibitors for metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitor effectiveness in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. One-year survival was 63% and one-year progression-free survival was 17%. Combining immunotherapy with other agents showed better results than immunotherapy alone, though outcomes remain modest overall.

items.title: Zoledronic acid protects bone health during enzalutamide plus ADT
items.summary: The BonEnza Phase 2 trial studied bone health in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients receiving enzalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy with or without zoledronic acid (a bone-protecting drug). After 18 months, patients receiving zoledronic acid had significantly less bone density loss and better preservation of bone quality compared to those without it.
